clue.text: Ceasefire due to a fog covering river, and the effect of freezing

indicators.note: the phrase 'a fog' sits over and around the river abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: mist is a thin fog
freezing water produces ice

explanation.surface: A weather report: fighting halted because of fog and a hard frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'due to' is only a link; 'covering' sets the fog phrase around the river letter, which lands just after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a formal agreement to stop fighting, i.e. a truce between warring sides.

clue.text: A spirit good for maturing

parts.note: gin is a spirit (alcoholic drink)

explanation.surface: A liquor improved by being left in the barrel to age.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe growing older and developing, as wine or cheese does over time.

clue.text: Earned right of choice in business making cake

parts.note: to have earned money is to have made it

indicators.note: the chosen letter is placed inside the word for business

parts.note: a line is a line of business, a trade

indicators.note: the right-hand end of the word choice, its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone who earned the right to choose in a firm, and baked a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A madeleine is a small French sponge cake, made famous by Proust.

clue.text: Uncast replacements?

parts.note: spares for a machine, but read as roles in a play that nobody has been cast in yet

explanation.surface: Replacement components that have not been moulded or cast.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is on 'part' as an acting role: a part not yet cast is spare.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare components replace worn ones; theatrical roles still unfilled are equally spare.

clue.text: Immigrant needing wages before end of year

indicators.note: the wages word comes before the final letter in answer order

parts.note: wages are income

indicators.note: the last letter of the word year

explanation.surface: A newcomer to the country who must have pay by the close of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: An incomer is someone who has moved into an area from elsewhere, a newcomer or settler.

clue.text: English motorway charge for land in east

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A toll on an English motorway, payable for land out east.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; the figure 1 is written as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a territory ruled by an emir, typically in the Middle East.

clue.text: A hearing finishing early in chambers

indicators.note: the trial stops one letter short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing

explanation.surface: A court hearing that ends ahead of time in a judge's chambers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing early' drops the L of TRIAL, leaving TRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are the upper chambers of the heart, or entrance halls in Roman houses.

clue.text: Ship of legend seeing freight skimmed

indicators.note: the top layer is taken off, so in this down clue the first letter goes

parts.note: cargo is freight

explanation.surface: A mythical vessel spotted with its load stripped off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the vessel of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth.

clue.text: Listener's up, accepting one's lift

indicators.note: the reversed listener takes the next piece inside it
in a down clue the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a listener is an ear; the 's stands for 'is' and links
one is I, and 's is S, giving 'I's'

explanation.surface: Someone who is listening perks up after taking a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Listener's' just means 'is'; 'up' reads the listener upwards, giving RAE, and 'accepting' takes in 'one's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it higher.

clue.text: Coils age in vehicles with no roof

indicators.note: the word for age goes inside the trimmed vehicles
in a down clue the top letter is removed

parts.note: cars are vehicles
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Coiled springs grow old inside convertible cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'age' is a verb here, not a period; 'with no roof' leaves ARS, and 'in' opens it after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Armatures are the wire-wound coils in a motor or generator.

clue.text: Certain dialects found around part of Asia

indicators.note: the letters are found spread around the run of two words, straddling them

explanation.surface: Some regional speech can be heard in an Asian region.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a large country in South Asia.

clue.text: Wrap cold fish and initially freeze it with lime, oddly

parts.note: ling is a fish of the cod family

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word freeze
the first, third and fifth letters of the run 'it lime'

explanation.surface: A recipe: wrap the cold fish and freeze it with some lime.
explanation.definitionFit: Cling film is thin plastic used to wrap food; a wrap of that kind.

clue.text: The moderation of relocating gaoled men north

indicators.note: the prisoners are moved around, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Moving imprisoned men to the north as a measured policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relocating' rearranges the nine letters of the prisoners, and the north letter follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden mean is the ideal middle way between extremes: moderation in all things.

clue.text: Experienced in soft fabric

definitions.meaning: underwent or sensed, past tense of feel
a matted cloth of pressed wool

explanation.surface: An expert in soft textiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of feel means experienced; separately, a pressed woollen cloth.

clue.text: Put up with mug and fish

parts.note: to lump it is to put up with something
a mug is a gullible person, a sucker

explanation.surface: Tolerating a mug and a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The lumpsucker is a round North Atlantic fish with a sucker on its belly.

clue.text: Into which mountain climbers may disappear?

definitions.text: Into which mountain climbers may disappear?

parts.words: Into which mountain climbers may disappear?
parts.note: people vanish into it in the idiom, and high altitude atmosphere is literally sparse

explanation.surface: Where climbers might go missing on a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: To vanish 'into thin air' is an idiom; mountaineers literally ascend into rarefied atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for vanishing without trace, also the low-oxygen atmosphere at altitude.

clue.text: Legal document for international meant to be played

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

indicators.note: the letters are played around with, rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal paper for an international fixture that is due to be played.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a will, a legal document disposing of property.

clue.text: Nation having trouble in developing cure

indicators.note: the trouble word sits inside the rearranged letters
the letters develop into a new form

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A country struggling to develop a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges the remedy to ECUR, and 'in' sets the trouble word between its U and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecuador is a country in South America on the equator.

clue.text: Part of court estates in area by river

parts.note: the dock is where the defendant stands in court
lands are estates

explanation.surface: A section of a court building's grounds lying near the river.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Docklands is the riverside district of former docks on the Thames.

clue.text: The girl has worried about time, and dresses

parts.note: she is a pronoun for a girl

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the time abbreviation
the letters are worried, shaken about

explanation.surface: The girl is anxious about time, and gets dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges HAS into AHS; 'about' puts T inside, giving ATHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheaths are close-fitting, straight-cut garments, so a kind of dress.

clue.text: Bear's hunger felt here

definitions.meaning: to bear, tolerate or put up with
the organ where a person feels hungry

explanation.surface: Where a bear feels its hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: To be able to tolerate something is to stand it; and hunger pangs come from the gut.

clue.text: Animals unfortunately carrying the majority of packs

indicators.note: the exclamation holds the shortened packs inside it

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

indicators.note: only most of the word packs is kept, its last two letters dropped

explanation.surface: Pack animals sadly bearing most of the load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' looks like an anagram signal but is the container word; 'the majority of' leaves three of five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpacas are South American camelids, kept for their wool.

clue.text: Statistician in reality having right to replace lines

indicators.note: the right abbreviation replaces the lines abbreviation

parts.note: actually means in reality

explanation.surface: A statistician who really has the right to replace some lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' is LL, the abbreviation for lines; 'to replace' swaps it for R.
explanation.definitionFit: An actuary is a statistician who calculates insurance risks and premiums.

clue.text: Weapon used to protect uranium plant

indicators.note: the weapon wraps around the uranium to protect it

parts.note: an arm is a weapon
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Arms used to guard uranium at a nuclear plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is a plant genus including cuckoo-pint and arum lilies.

clue.text: Sore, but pulls clear reducing the odds

indicators.note: the odd letters of the phrase are removed, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Painful, but a gambler draws clear of the field as odds shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is an open sore on the skin or a mucous membrane.

clue.text: Left on board, gather one's entry may be barred by this

definitions.text: entry may be barred by this

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
to cull is to gather or select
one is I, and 's is S

explanation.surface: A sailor told to collect what is his, but the door may be locked.
explanation.definitionFit: A portcullis is the heavy grille lowered to block a castle gateway.

clue.text: Authority, for example, Scot regularly ignored

parts.note: say means for example

indicators.note: every other letter of Scot is dropped, keeping the first and third

explanation.surface: Authority, such as a Scotsman routinely overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Say-so means the power or permission to decide something.

clue.text: Struggle with opinion

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

explanation.surface: Wrestling with a point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a personal opinion.

clue.text: Dish a client had suffered, with no end of salt

indicators.note: the letters suffer, getting knocked out of order
the final letter of salt is taken away from the pool
the end of a word is its final letter, so only the closing letter of salt is meant

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer was ill after an unsalted dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffered' rearranges ACLIENTHAD; 'with no' removes the T, the end of salt.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican rolled tortilla with a filling.

clue.text: Unconventional black king taking precedence

indicators.note: the king letter goes first, ahead of the black word

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
inky means black

explanation.surface: An unusual chess move where the black king goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinky means bizarre or unusual, especially in tastes.

clue.text: Cast finished on the radio

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard, not seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: through means finished

explanation.surface: A cast's broadcast is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Threw is the past tense of throw, and cast as a verb means threw.

clue.text: The osprey flies as if by magic

indicators.note: the bird flies around, scattering its letters

explanation.surface: The bird of prey takes off as if conjured by a magician.
explanation.definitionFit: Hey presto is the conjuror's exclamation when a trick suddenly works.
